questions.tag: United States of America · Monetary policy
questions.q: What action did the Federal Reserve take regarding its benchmark interest rate?
o: It increased the rate for the first time in three years.
It decreased the rate to combat an economic slowdown.
It left the rate unchanged to match the Bank of England.
It suspended the rate-setting process due to executive pressure.
questions.e: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate for the first time in a three-year period, demonstrating its independence from executive branch pressure. The other options contradict this specific tightening move.

questions.q: How did the Bank of England respond to rising inflation figures regarding its benchmark interest rate?
o: It prepared to leave the rate unchanged at 3.75%.
It raised the rate immediately to match the Federal Reserve.
It lowered the rate to stimulate domestic credit creation.
It abandoned the interest rate target entirely.
questions.e: The Bank of England planned to hold its benchmark rate at 3.75% despite rising inflation figures, decoupling from other central banks. Lowering or raising the rate misstates the announced policy path.
